languages.name: Japanese
languages.notes: Standard Japanese (Hyōjungo) based on the Tokyo dialect; taught in all schools and used by all media.

languages.name: Ryukyuan languages
languages.notes: A group of six related languages in Okinawa and Amami (Okinawan, Kunigami, Miyako, Yaeyama, Yonaguni, Amami). UNESCO lists all as endangered.

languages.name: Ainu
languages.notes: Indigenous language of Hokkaido; critically endangered with fewer than 100 fluent native speakers. Active revitalisation efforts.

languages.name: English
languages.notes: Spoken by a minority; more common in central Tokyo, major hotels, international business, and younger residents.

languages.name: Mandarin Chinese
languages.notes: Largest resident foreign-language community; concentrated in Tokyo, Osaka, Yokohama.

languages.name: Korean
languages.notes: Includes Zainichi Koreans (multi-generational residents) and recent migrants.

languages.name: Vietnamese
languages.notes: Fast-growing community via technical intern and specified-skilled-worker programs.

languages.name: Portuguese
languages.notes: Brazilian Portuguese, concentrated in factory towns of Aichi, Shizuoka, Gunma.

languages.name: Tagalog / Filipino
languages.notes: Largely in service industries and healthcare.

languages.name: Nepali
languages.notes: Large community in and around Tokyo; second-largest non-Japanese school-age population in several wards.

languages.name: Japanese Sign Language
languages.notes: Native sign language of the Japanese Deaf community; recognised in law and used by ~320,000 people.

english_proficiency.notes: Tokyo scores higher than the national average; big hotels, major museums, Shinkansen announcements, and Google Translate's camera mode cover most gaps for visitors.
